newsitem.title: USA: Mercantile sees deal adding to earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mercantile sees deal adding to earnings.

text.p: Mercantile Bancorp Inc on Monday said it expected its proposed $1.07 billion acquisition of Roosevelt Financial Group Inc to add to earnings as soon as the deal closed in the second quarter of next year.
The $18.2 billion bank holding company also said it expected to take an after-tax, merger-related charge of $25 million to $30 million charge in the second quarter.
Overall, Mercantile said it expected the deal to add $0.28 a share to 1997 earnings in the third and fourth quarters and $0.69 in 1998.
Mercantile plans to save $20.2 million a year in occupancy and branch costs but did not tell reporters at a news conference how many branches it would close.
"There will be some certainly but probably fewer than you might think on the face value of it," Mercantile Chief Executive Thomas Jacobsen said.
The banks also said that because of attrition, as well as the fact that the two companies will not be completely combined, layoffs could be minimal.
"We're not aware of anyone at this time that won't be able to find a role with the ongoing company," said Stanley Bradshaw, chief executive at Roosevelt.
Mercantile, which also expects an $855 million merger with Mark Twain Bancshares Inc to close in the second quarter of 1997, did not rule out future acquisitions.

"We have continuing interest in Illinois, Iowa and Arkansas," said John Beirise, group vice president for emerging markets at Mercantile. "Oklahoma has interest to us and would also be a logical extension."
Mercantile shares were down 7/8 to 49-7/8, while Roosevelt rose 2-3/8 to 20-1/2 in early afternoon trading.
